content: One cannot think well, love well, sleep well, if one has not dined well.
author: Virginia Woolf
sourceWork: A Room of One's Own (1929), Chapter 1
story: Delivering two lectures to female undergraduates at Newnham and Girton Colleges at Cambridge, Woolf famously compared the lavish banquet served at the men's college with the austere, bland dinner offered at the women's institution. With wry irony, she illuminated the foundational physical reality underpinning intellectual life: philosophy and creativity cannot flourish when the body is starved, neglected, or exhausted.
reflectionPrompt: How well are you tending to the basic physical nourishment, rest, and atmosphere required to support your highest mental clarity?
